title: Palbociclib with endocrine therapy
context_label: HR-positive, HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer
schedule_summary: Take palbociclib for 21 days, then have 7 days without palbociclib. The aromatase-inhibitor tablet continues every day, or fulvestrant injections follow their separate schedule. The week off applies to palbociclib, not automatically to the hormone treatment.
purpose: Palbociclib slows cell-cycle progression while the hormone partner reduces oestrogen signalling. The aim in this advanced-disease pathway is cancer control, with treatment and response reviewed over time.
indication_text: NCCP 00414 a: HR-positive, HER2-negative locally advanced/metastatic disease with an aromatase inhibitor. NCCP 00414 b: the same receptor/disease setting with fulvestrant in women who have received prior endocrine therapy. Pre/perimenopausal women also need an agreed ovarian-suppression plan.
administration_text: Check whether the pharmacy supplied capsules or tablets: capsules are taken with food; tablets can be taken with or without food. Swallow whole at a consistent time. Avoid grapefruit. If you miss or vomit a dose, do not take an extra dose; take the next scheduled dose. Do not restart after a clinical hold until the treating team confirms.
monitoring_summary: Before the first dose: FBC, kidney and liver bloods; review other medicines, pregnancy possibility, receptor results, menopausal status and the exact endocrine partner. Confirm ovarian suppression when relevant. FBC on Day 1 and Day 15 of cycles 1–2, then Day 1 from cycle 3. Kidney/liver bloods before each cycle. If counts are low, extra blood tests and a pause may be needed. Only after no worse than grade 1/2 neutropenia in the first 6 cycles may FBC frequency reduce to every 3 months before a cycle, with additional tests when clinically indicated.
review_status: Source-reconciled development content; independent oncology, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

agents.name: Palbociclib
agents.mechanism: Blocks cell-cycle signals that help cancer cells divide
agents.explanation: Hormone signalling can activate cyclin-D/CDK4/6. Palbociclib blocks this control point, helping keep susceptible cells from progressing through the cell cycle. Combining it with endocrine therapy acts on both the hormonal signal and downstream cell division.
agents.watch: The key early issue is a falling white-cell count, which may cause no symptoms. Keep blood-test appointments and report infection symptoms or new cough/breathlessness promptly.
risks: Rare but serious interstitial lung disease / pneumonitis

agents.name: Your endocrine partner
agents.type: Either an aromatase inhibitor or fulvestrant
agents.mechanism: Reduces oestrogen signalling to hormone-sensitive cells
visual: AI lowers oestrogen; fulvestrant targets its receptor
agents.explanation: An aromatase inhibitor lowers oestrogen production; fulvestrant acts at the oestrogen receptor. These are alternative partners here, not an instruction to take both. The partner’s dose, monitoring and injection or tablet schedule must be confirmed.
agents.watch: Discuss joint/hot-flush and bone symptoms with an AI, or injection-site/bleeding symptoms with fulvestrant. Pre/perimenopausal women require ovarian suppression in the prescribed combination.
risks: Hot flushes and other hormone-related symptoms
AI: joint symptoms and bone loss
Partner-specific liver, interaction and pregnancy considerations

monitoring_schedule.note: Reference timing, not booked appointments. Ask who requests each test, when it is due, who reviews the result and whom to contact if it is missing. Delays can change cycle numbers; time-based monitoring remains time-based.

urgent_extra: Contact the treatment team promptly if you feel feverish or unwell, have shaking chills or infection symptoms, or develop new cough or breathlessness. Follow the local emergency temperature instructions; do not wait for a planned blood test or for the 38.5°C value used in one clinician dose-adjustment table. Severe breathing difficulty needs emergency care.

sections.title: Two treatments with different clocks
sections.text: An aromatase inhibitor is taken continuously. If fulvestrant is the partner, the usual 500 mg injection schedule is Days 1, 15 and 29 initially, then every 28 days under NCCP scheduling. Injection dose and tolerability need their own clinical review. Ovarian-suppression injections, if needed, have another prescribed schedule.

sections.title: The first two cycles need an extra blood test
sections.text: The Day 15 blood count checks for early marrow suppression. A Day 22 repeat may be requested after a low Day 15 count. The team interprets the result and tells you whether to continue or pause.

sections.title: The week off and next prescription
sections.text: Days 22–28 are the planned palbociclib rest week. Arrange the next blood test and supply in advance. The team may draw pre-cycle bloods locally before Day 1; the exact appointment is a local arrangement, not a universal Day 25/26 rule.

sections.title: New medicines and formulations
sections.text: Tell the oncology pharmacist about antibiotics, antifungals, supplements and herbal medicines. Avoid St John’s Wort and grapefruit. Food instructions differ for capsules and tablets, so check the dispensed box.

sections.title: Visits and access
sections.text: Palbociclib itself is an oral treatment and does not require a port or infusion pump. Fulvestrant or ovarian-suppression partners require injection visits. Do not infer that these visits stop during the palbociclib rest week.

evidence.title: PALOMA-2, palbociclib + letrozole: EMA efficacy tables 6 and 8
evidence.population: 666 postmenopausal patients with HR-positive/HER2-negative advanced breast cancer without prior systemic treatment for advanced disease; 444 palbociclib/letrozole vs 222 placebo/letrozole.
evidence.primary_endpoint: Investigator-assessed PFS at the 2016 primary analysis: 24.8 vs 14.5 months; HR 0.576 (95% CI 0.463–0.718).
evidence.interpretation: Investigator-assessed PFS at the 2016 primary analysis: 24.8 vs 14.5 months; HR 0.576 (95% CI 0.463–0.718). Adding palbociclib delayed progression in the studied population.
evidence.limitations: PFS is not survival. Final overall survival was not statistically significant: 53.9 vs 51.2 months; HR 0.956 (95% CI 0.777–1.177), p=0.6755, cutoff 15 November 2021. Do not present this as a proven OS benefit.

teachback: Which medicine is taken or given when, what checks are expected next, and which symptoms mean you should call today?
consent_support: The same low count can lead to a different action at Day 1 and Day 15 of the first two cycles. Dose decisions also depend on fever/infection, recovery, severity and current dose. A clinician must confirm a restart; the patient timeline is an explanation, not permission to self-adjust treatment. Do not use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. EMA specifies effective contraception during treatment and for at least 3 weeks after the last dose for women and 14 weeks for men; the endocrine partner may require a longer interval. Discuss fertility preservation before treatment when relevant.

support.title: Nausea support
support.text: Palbociclib is classified as oral minimal–low emetic risk. Routine premedication is not usually needed; discuss rescue medication if nausea occurs. A generic intensive chemotherapy antiemetic schedule is not automatically added.

support.title: Low counts and infection
support.text: Blood-count monitoring, dose interruption and dose reduction are central to support. Growth-factor use is an individual clinical decision, not an automatic routine injection on this card.

support.title: Hormone-related symptoms
support.text: Discuss hot flushes, joint symptoms, vaginal symptoms, sleep and bone health according to the actual endocrine partner. Support can be adjusted without silently changing either cancer medicine.

support.title: Mouth, bowel and energy symptoms
support.text: Report mouth soreness, troublesome nausea/diarrhoea or fatigue so supportive treatment and hydration can be reviewed. New breathing symptoms must not be dismissed as expected fatigue.

timeline_note: Treatment days are specified by the regimen. Symptom timing varies; the full-cycle symptom bands show that an effect can occur at any point, not a measured probability or severity.

chronology_notes.text: Take palbociclib for 21 days, then have 7 days without palbociclib. The aromatase-inhibitor tablet continues every day, or fulvestrant injections follow their separate schedule. The week off applies to palbociclib, not automatically to the hormone treatment.

chronology_notes.title: Tests and appointments
chronology_notes.text: Use the monitoring table for baseline and later checks. A rest week does not remove infection or other risks.

safety_note: Contact the treatment team promptly if you feel feverish or unwell, have shaking chills or infection symptoms, or develop new cough or breathlessness. Follow the local emergency temperature instructions; do not wait for a planned blood test or for the 38.5°C value used in one clinician dose-adjustment table. Severe breathing difficulty needs emergency care.

chapters.title: The exact treatment being discussed
chapters.intro: Palbociclib slows cell-cycle progression while the hormone partner reduces oestrogen signalling. The aim in this advanced-disease pathway is cancer control, with treatment and response reviewed over time.

items.title: Who this covers
items.text: NCCP 00414 a: HR-positive, HER2-negative locally advanced/metastatic disease with an aromatase inhibitor. NCCP 00414 b: the same receptor/disease setting with fulvestrant in women who have received prior endocrine therapy. Pre/perimenopausal women also need an agreed ovarian-suppression plan.

items.title: Dose and administration
items.text: Usual palbociclib dose: 125 mg once daily on Days 1–21 of a 28-day cycle; reduced prescribed doses are 100 mg or 75 mg.. Check whether the pharmacy supplied capsules or tablets: capsules are taken with food; tablets can be taken with or without food. Swallow whole at a consistent time. Avoid grapefruit. If you miss or vomit a dose, do not take an extra dose; take the next scheduled dose. Do not restart after a clinical hold until the treating team confirms.

items.title: Duration and decisions
items.text: Treatment continues while it is helping and side effects remain acceptable. There is no fixed adjuvant course in NCCP 00414. Blood results or symptoms may change the dose or postpone the next cycle.

items.title: Individual safety and source differences
items.text: The same low count can lead to a different action at Day 1 and Day 15 of the first two cycles. Dose decisions also depend on fever/infection, recovery, severity and current dose. A clinician must confirm a restart; the patient timeline is an explanation, not permission to self-adjust treatment.

chapters.title: Checks throughout treatment
chapters.intro: Blood tests assess treatment safety. Scans assess disease or investigate symptoms. Echo and ECG answer different questions.

items.title: Before treatment
items.text: Before the first dose: FBC, kidney and liver bloods; review other medicines, pregnancy possibility, receptor results, menopausal status and the exact endocrine partner. Confirm ovarian suppression when relevant.

items.title: During treatment
items.text: FBC on Day 1 and Day 15 of cycles 1–2, then Day 1 from cycle 3. Kidney/liver bloods before each cycle. If counts are low, extra blood tests and a pause may be needed. Only after no worse than grade 1/2 neutropenia in the first 6 cycles may FBC frequency reduce to every 3 months before a cycle, with additional tests when clinically indicated.

items.title: Heart checks
items.text: Palbociclib does not have the routine ECG timetable used for ribociclib. ECG or echo is arranged if symptoms, another medicine or individual cardiac risk make it appropriate.

items.title: Bone health
items.text: Bone-health monitoring belongs to the endocrine partner, ovarian suppression and personal fracture risk. If taking an aromatase inhibitor, agree the baseline bone-density assessment and follow-up plan with the team; palbociclib itself has no fixed DXA interval.

chapters.title: Your wider treatment plan
chapters.intro: Additional treatments depend on the confirmed setting and indication.

items.title: Advanced-disease scans
items.text: Response assessment in advanced breast cancer is generally every two to four months, adapted to disease dynamics, sites, symptoms and treatment. Less frequent monitoring may suit indolent disease. New symptoms or suspected progression need earlier assessment. The team chooses the imaging method; this is not an automatic three-month CT chest/abdomen/pelvis order.

items.title: Tumour markers
items.text: If informative, particularly when elevated at baseline or disease is not readily measurable, tumour markers may supplement clinical assessment and imaging. A marker rise alone should not trigger a treatment change. There is no universal fixed marker timetable.

items.title: Pregnancy, fertility and contraception
items.text: Do not use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. EMA specifies effective contraception during treatment and for at least 3 weeks after the last dose for women and 14 weeks for men; the endocrine partner may require a longer interval. Discuss fertility preservation before treatment when relevant.

chapters.title: Evidence depends on the population
chapters.intro: Different studies answer different questions; do not compare their results as if populations and follow-up were identical.

items.title: PALOMA-3, palbociclib + fulvestrant: EMA efficacy table 9
items.text: 521 patients with HR-positive/HER2-negative advanced cancer after endocrine progression; 347 palbociclib/fulvestrant vs 174 placebo/fulvestrant, with ovarian suppression for pre/perimenopausal women. Updated investigator-assessed PFS, 23 October 2015 cutoff: 11.2 vs 4.6 months; HR 0.497 (95% CI 0.398–0.620). Adding palbociclib improved PFS after prior endocrine therapy. The prespecified final OS analysis was not statistically significant: 34.9 vs 28.0 months; HR 0.814 (95% CI 0.644–1.029). Separate later exploratory follow-up from this final analysis; do not compare PFS numerically with PALOMA-2 as if populations matched.
